name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,604

clue.text: Direction of take-off in this plane!

definitions.text: Direction of take-off in this plane!

blocks.note: surface reading: which way an aeroplane heads when it leaves the runway
setter's reading: 'plane' is the geometric plane of the grid entry itself, a down light, and a jump jet climbs straight up

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' seems to mean an aircraft, but it also means a geometric plane; this entry is a down light, so its own plane is upright, and jump jets take off straight upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight up is the direction both of a jump jet's lift-off and of every down entry in a crossword grid.

clue.text: Understanding directions about shelter put up in centre

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece is placed around another
in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: east-north-east, a compass direction built from three points
a tent is a canvas shelter
put down or placed, past tense
the core is the centre of something

explanation.surface: Someone grasps instructions for building a shelter in the middle of a camp.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'directions' are one three-point compass bearing, not instructions; in a down entry 'put up' means the word is read upward. The phrase is French, borrowed into English diplomacy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Entente Cordiale was the 1904 Anglo-French agreement, and the phrase now means any friendly mutual accord between nations.

clue.text: Songbird catching a cold becomes silent

indicators.note: catching something means taking hold of it, so one piece grips the others inside

blocks.note: the tit is a small songbird
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A bird catches a chill and loses its voice.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the bird falls silent from illness; really the two small pieces sit inside the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means unspoken or understood without words, as in tacit agreement, a close synonym for silent.

clue.text: Boy singer with his rector for excitement

indicators.note: excitement stirs things up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A choirboy thrills alongside the vicar of his parish.
explanation.walkthrough: The rector suggests a church setting that fits the answer, which helps hide that his name is the raw letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorister is a member of a church choir, traditionally a boy treble in English cathedrals.

clue.text: Girl guzzling due to drain coffee cups

indicators.note: draining a vessel empties out its contents, so only the outside letters remain
to cup something is to hold it in curved hands, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: the word with its middle letter emptied out
a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: A girl is gulping her drink because she needs to finish her coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coffee cups' reads as crockery, but 'cups' is a verb: the coffee holds the emptied word. A ladette is British slang for a young woman who drinks hard and rowdily.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladette is a young woman given to boisterous heavy drinking, so a hard-drinking girl is a fair description.

clue.text: Good man with something to cover flasher at disco?

blocks.note: a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST
a robe is a garment to cover the body

explanation.surface: A decent fellow hands over a coat to hide an exhibitionist at a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flasher' suggests a man exposing himself, which the cover joke plays on; really it is a light that flashes.
explanation.definitionFit: A strobe light pulses rapid bright bursts, a fixture of dance floors, so it flashes at discos.

clue.text: Rocket incorporating new submarine detection system

indicators.note: incorporating means taking into the body of something, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: to rocket is to soar upward, as prices do
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A missile fitted with a fresh system for spotting submarines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocket' looks like a noun for a weapon, but it is the verb meaning to shoot up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonar uses sound pulses echoing underwater to locate objects, and navies rely on it to find submarines.

clue.text: Cut wood supporting seats

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece that supports another sits beneath it, fixing the order

blocks.note: the seat is the backside, so seats are rumps
teak is a hardwood

explanation.surface: Timber is sawn to make the frames that hold up chairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a verb about sawing wood, but it is a noun: a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rump steak is a particular cut of beef taken from the hindquarters, so it is one cut from a butcher.

clue.text: Substance got him dancing in swimwear

indicators.note: dancing moves things about, so the letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Some drug has got a man dancing at a pool party in his trunks.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a story of intoxication; three whole words supply exactly the fifteen letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathing costume is the British term for a swimsuit, so the plural phrase is a set of swimming garments.

clue.text: Potassium density fluctuates with force and atomic explosive

indicators.note: to fluctuate is to shift up and down unsteadily, so the letters shift around

blocks.note: K is the chemical symbol for potassium
taken as written
F is the symbol for force in physics
taken as written

explanation.surface: A physics or chemistry note: a potassium compound's density varies, combining with force and atomic energy to explode.
explanation.walkthrough: The scientific vocabulary disguises two symbols and two whole words, all mixed together; the indicator sits in the middle but covers every piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick of dynamite is the standard cylindrical unit of that blasting explosive, so it is an explosive item.

clue.text: Difficult problem for Ravel

blocks.note: surface reading: a hard task facing the French composer Maurice Ravel
setter's reading: to ravel is to tangle or untangle threads, and a tangle is a hard problem to unpick

explanation.walkthrough: The capital R makes Ravel the composer of Bolero; really it is the ordinary verb for tangling and untangling, and the answer is both a tangle and a hard problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot is literally a tangle to be unpicked and figuratively an intricate difficulty, as in a knotty problem.

clue.text: Work experience aboard vessel protecting marine species

indicators.note: to protect something is to shield it all round, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: aboard a vessel means in it
a ship is a sea vessel
the tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A trainee spends time on a conservation ship guarding sea creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marine species' suggests fish or whales, but the creature is a seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: An internship is a temporary placement in which a trainee gains practical experience of a job.

clue.text: Theatre skill doubled energy in comic dialogue

blocks.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
an art is a skill
E for energy, twice

explanation.surface: An actor's craft gives double the energy to a comic double act.
explanation.walkthrough: Rep is the repertory theatre company, a stock abbreviation in British crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick, witty back-and-forth conversation, the banter that drives comedy exchanges.

clue.text: Taking it all in having gone round planet?

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so one piece is wrapped around another

blocks.note: someone who has gone is absent
an orb is a sphere, poetic for a planet

explanation.surface: A space traveller soaking up every sight after circling the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone round planet' suggests orbiting, but 'having gone' is one piece and 'round' is the wrapping instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Absorbent describes something that soaks up liquid, or figuratively takes in everything around it.

clue.text: Solemn promise to refrain from drinking toast

definitions.text: Solemn promise to refrain from drinking

blocks.clueFragment: Solemn promise to refrain from drinking
blocks.note: first meaning: a temperance vow, the formal oath to give up alcohol
second meaning: an old verb for drinking someone's health

explanation.surface: A teetotal vow is undermined by raising a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the same word is both swearing off drink and drinking to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The pledge is a temperance vow of abstinence, and archaically to pledge someone was to drink their health.

clue.text: Mixed responses but continues forward

indicators.note: mixed things are jumbled together, so the letters come out in another order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A project gets lukewarm feedback yet carries on regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed responses' reads as a stock phrase about reviews, which hides the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To press on is a phrasal verb meaning to keep going determinedly, so its third-person form matches.

clue.text: Second customer calling for house cat

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a user is a customer of a service

explanation.surface: A returning shopper asks for a domestic cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal describing the customer, but it is the short time, colloquially a mo.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouser is a cat kept for catching mice, the job of a working household cat.

clue.text: Smoke hid rocky Arab territory

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady and shaken, so the letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Smoke conceals a stony stretch of desert land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' fits the desert picture so naturally it passes as plain description.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheikdom is a land ruled by a sheik, the title of an Arab chief or ruler.

clue.text: Daily porridge needed for African flier

blocks.note: The Sun is a British daily newspaper
porridge and bird are both British slang for a prison sentence

explanation.surface: Someone eats oatmeal every morning before flying from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porridge' suggests oats, but in British slang it is jail time, as is bird (from rhyming slang bird-lime, time). The Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunbirds are small nectar-feeding birds found chiefly in Africa, so this is a flying creature of that continent.

clue.text: Revolutionary and monster becoming accessories

indicators.note: a revolutionary overturns the existing order, so the letters are overturned and reordered

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebel and a beast turn into fashion trinkets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a person, the first of two characters; it is the instruction applied to the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Adornments are decorative additions such as jewellery, much like accessories worn to complete an outfit.

clue.text: Be consumed in chimney erected for tycoon

indicators.note: being in something means lying within it, so one piece sits inside another
something erected is stood upright, and in a down entry that turns the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: lum is a Scottish and northern English word for a chimney
money that goes is consumed or used up

explanation.surface: Something is burnt up in a newly built chimney for a business magnate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be consumed' suggests burning in the chimney, but it means to be used up. Lum is a dialect word for chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: A mogul is a powerful magnate in business or media, after the Mughal emperors, so a direct synonym.

clue.text: Horse to follow flawlessly finding way through

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this piece is placed behind the next

blocks.note: to know something pat is to have it perfectly, without a slip
H is slang for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: A horse trails behind another perfectly as it picks its route.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse and H are both slang for heroin, which links them. Pat as an adverb means exactly or perfectly memorised.
explanation.definitionFit: A path is a track or route that lets you pass through somewhere, such as a field or wood.

clue.text: Film company sorry having removed jerk

indicators.note: removing something takes it out, so part of the word is cut away

blocks.note: a sorry state is a pitiful one
a tic is an involuntary twitch or jerk

explanation.surface: A studio apologises after firing an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' wants to be an insult for a person, but it is a sudden twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathé is a long-established French film production and distribution company, famous for its newsreels.

clue.text: People opposed to the enemy are in a rush

blocks.note: a race is a people or nation
to be against something is to oppose it
time is often called the enemy, as in the saying

explanation.surface: A resistance movement is hurrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The enemy' suggests a hostile army, but it is the stock phrase for time running out.
explanation.definitionFit: A race against time is a desperate hurry to finish something before a deadline arrives.

clue.text: Payment letter demands material about conservationists

indicators.note: being about something means surrounding it, so one piece is placed around another

blocks.note: material means real, physical rather than imagined
the National Trust, a British conservation charity that looks after historic houses and land

explanation.surface: A bill arrives demanding money for fabric relating to green campaigners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like correspondence but means a landlord, someone who lets property; 'material' looks like cloth but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Rental is the money paid to a landlord for use of property, exactly what one who lets requires.

clue.text: Performer takes action to return in Hamlet?

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the letters run backwards
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: to sue is to take legal action
Hamlet is Shakespeare's Prince of Denmark, so a Dane

explanation.surface: An actor is called back on stage during a performance of the Shakespeare tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make Hamlet the play, but the piece needed is its hero, the Dane.
explanation.definitionFit: A danseuse is a female ballet dancer, one kind of stage performer, from the French word.
